business_problem: Breast Cancer Canada needed a secure, ethics-approved cloud environment that could collect long-term patient-reported data and also help translate complex pathology information into plain language without the limitations of antiquated university-hosted infrastructure.
solution_summary: Breast Cancer Canada partnered with CloudifyAI to rebuild its patient advocacy and research platform on Google Cloud so long-term patient-reported outcomes could be collected, analyzed, and converted into clinically credible evidence. BigQuery provides the analytics backbone for large, multi-point datasets gathered through the PROgress Tracker 2.0 study, while Cloud Run, Pub/Sub, Google Apps Script, Cloud Logging, and Cloud Monitoring support the surrounding application services. On top of that secure environment, CONNECT lets patients upload pathology reports, and Google Cloud AI tools perform OCR and document interpretation so medical language can be translated into understandable treatment timelines and question prompts. Gemini Notebook is also used to transform internal educational materials into clearer patient roadmaps. This architecture gave BCC an ethically compliant clinical-study platform for research publication, multi-site adoption, and a future national registry.

data_flow: Patient-reported outcomes and uploaded pathology reports enter BCC's cloud study environment, are processed and analyzed through BigQuery-backed services, translated into readable explanations and timelines through AI-assisted document interpretation, and then reused for research, advocacy, and multi-site clinical decision support.
business_outcome: Breast Cancer Canada scaled PROgress Tracker 2.0 past 1,000 active patients, published research at ASCO, expanded adoption across hospital sites, and gained a secure data foundation for advocacy, future wearables integration, and potential national-registry use.
